subject: Fleet health & deal snapshots — weekly triage
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 6 Dec 2029 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fleet health & deal snapshots — weekly triage

Morning team — attaching the latest fleet snapshot for this week (see attachment). Quick summary and asks so we can close the loop in the stand: 

Key active deals this week:
- Altura Health (Samir): pilot target 2029-12-20; ask = 8 reserved GPUs + 120k token bursts/week for 6 weeks. They need predictable latency for model evaluation and want a canary by 12/13.
- Nimbus AI (Lydia): pilot running; expected scale request 4 reserved GPUs starting week of 12/27, uncertain on commit length.
- ACME (procurement): still negotiating SLA credits; likely Q1 reserve ask but pricing/terms blocking.

Operational health highlights from spreadsheet:
- Current reserved utilization: 72% across US pools.
- Burst slot headroom: 18% immediate, additional 12% via preemptible scaling on night windows.
- KV-cache hit improvement after quantization tests reduced token cost ~9% for common prefixes.

Asks (short):
1) Ben/infra: confirm if we can guarantee 8 reserved slots for Altura by 12/13 for the canary (even if ephemeral with fallback policy). If not, propose exact fallback model variant and latency expectations.
2) Laura/finance: confirm whether we can offer a 3-week trial at reduced commit (commit -> reserved holdback) and what credit exposure looks like.
3) Marissa/sales: please confirm the mutual action plan milestones Samir expects and whether he can sign a PO for a 6-week pilot.

Attachments: 2029-12-06_fleet_snapshot.xlsx (weekly sheet), Altura_MutualActionPlan_Dec2029.pdf (draft MAP).

If we can get answers before the 11:30 sync I’ll update the action column and push a short runbook for the canary.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 6 Dec 2029 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet health & deal snapshots — weekly triage

On Fri, Dec 6, 2029 at 9:02 AM Jordan Blake wrote:
> Morning team — attaching the latest fleet snapshot for this week (see attachment). Quick summary and asks so we can close the loop in the stand:
>
> Key active deals this week:
> - Altura Health (Samir): pilot target 2029-12-20; ask = 8 reserved GPUs + 120k token bursts/week for 6 weeks. They need predictable latency for model evaluation and want a canary by 12/13.

Thanks Jordan — short responses inline.

- Altura: I’ll push Samir to sign the MAP today; if we get the PO we can treat the 8 GPUs as short-term reserved with a 2-week notice window. We should still plan for fallback routing to a 4-GPU quantized variant if utilization spikes.

- Nimbus: good to keep them on the QA pool; Ben, can we keep a warm 1-2 GPU buffer for quick scale? Their model gives high KV-cache reuse so cost impact is lower.

Action: I’ll update the MAP with a firm canary milestone (12/13) and ask Samir for PO by EOD. If finance needs a trial structure, Laura I’m happy to align on credits + escalation clause.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-ops@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Dec 2029 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet health & deal snapshots — weekly triage

Marissa / team — dug into the snapshot and the ask. TL;DR: we can meet the 8-GPU canary for Altura on 12/13 with these caveats:

- Current pool headroom: we have 9 spare reserved-class GPUs if we accept a 48-hour rebalancing window. Guaranteed latency only possible if we prioritize their traffic on pool A (west-us-low-latency).
- If ACME SLA negotiation increases reserved demand this month, we’d need to re-evaluate on Mon 12/16 and potentially move Altura to a quantized 4-GPU profile temporarily.
- Burst tokens: we can provision 120k token/week by staging KV-cache hotshots and enabling daytime burst pools. That adds ~7% tail latency risk on peak days.

Proposed steps:
1) Allocate 8 GPUs from west-us pool A for 12/13-12/20 (short hold) — requires PO or signed MAP to lock; otherwise we mark as provisional.
2) Prepare a fallback runbook to route to 4-GPU quantized variant and activate preemptible burst slots (documented in the runbook link).
3) Run a canary 12/13 at 10:00 PST with synthetic load (Jordan, please confirm test data).

Attachment: small runbook stub referenced in the spreadsheet (tab: "Altura-canar y-runbook").

—Ben
Ben Carter
VP Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: finance-sales@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Dec 2029 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet health & deal snapshots — weekly triage

Thanks all — quick finance readout:

- Trial credit framework: We can approve a 3-week reduced-commit trial with a conditional credit of up to 35% of weekly reserved fees, capped at $60k, provided we have a signed MAP and a PO with expected conversion milestones.
- Exposure: If Altura runs full 8 GPUs for 6 weeks without conversion, cost exposure to Redwood ~ $98k (net of recommended credits). Recommend adding a mid-pilot checkpoint at week 2 to re-evaluate.

Requests for sales/ops:
1) Get the signed MAP/PO by EOD to convert allocation from provisional to reserved.
2) Ben: add a short cost-alert threshold (e.g., 120% of forecasted token burn) so finance gets notified before overrun.

If the MAP is signed today, finance will provision the trial credit and mark the funds in our Q4 runway.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference

[Attachment references: 2029-12-06_fleet_snapshot.xlsx; Altura_MutualActionPlan_Dec2029.pdf]
